messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy fanout started -> env=production, tag=release-1.8.2, commit=abc1234, services=[runtime, api, console], canary=10%

peter.l: ack, watching. tagging this release in #incidents if anything pops

maya.s: release notes https://releases.redwood.com/1.8.2 — contains runtime perf fixes and api schema change (breaking for old clients)

deploy-bot: runtime: STARTING
api: STARTING
console: STARTING

kat.devops: FYI rolling canary 10% -> 50% if green

deploy-bot: runtime: SUCCESS (instances: 12/12) 
api: UNSTABLE - failing healthchecks on 2/5 canaries
console: SUCCESS

peter.l: api flapping on healthcheck, logs show 500s with `KeyError: 'user_id'` after schema validation change

oncall-jess: taking this, pulling logs and the failing canary pod

oncall-jess: quick note — looks like a schema mismatch between sdk clients pinned to v1.8.1 and new api expects `user_id` in header; exposing 500s. Reverting api to previous image

deploy-bot: api: ROLLBACK initiated -> target image=release-1.8.1 commit=def5678

deploy-bot: api: ROLLBACK COMPLETE (all canaries replaced)

deploy-bot: FINAL STATUS -> runtime: SUCCESS, api: ROLLBACK_SUCCESS (serving release-1.8.1), console: SUCCESS

maya.s: OK. reverting pinned api in canary config. will open follow-up PR to add migration note + stricter schema gate

peter.l: creating a short post-deploy ticket and tagging eng-ml for validation. moving this to postmortems if needed. :white_check_mark:

kat.devops: can we keep the release tag `release-1.8.2` but mark api as not-yet-deployed in prod?

deploy-bot: release-1.8.2 tag preserved, api marked `deferred` in release registry. Canary window closed.

oncall-jess: thanks all, escalations cleared. I'll put a short blameless note in the ticket.
